description: Golden evaluation set for AAIE_011_HLC Hospital Policy & SOP Assistant. References AC-08/AC-09/AC-10. 20 answerable questions + 2 deliberate out-of-scope questions to test the abstention path (AC-05).

items.question: How long must alcohol-based hand rub be applied for during routine hand hygiene?
items.reference_answer: Alcohol-based hand rub (ABHR) must be applied for a minimum of 20 seconds, covering all hand surfaces.

items.question: What is the correct PPE doffing sequence and where must it occur?
items.reference_answer: Doff in this order: gloves, hand hygiene, gown, hand hygiene, eye protection, respirator, hand hygiene. Doffing must occur at the anteroom, not inside the patient room, except for the respirator.

items.question: What negative-pressure and respirator requirements apply under Airborne Precautions?
items.reference_answer: Airborne Precautions require a negative-pressure room and a fit-tested N95/FFP2 respirator for all entrants.

items.question: Within what timeframe must a PPE breach be reported, and to whom?
items.reference_answer: A suspected PPE breach must be reported to the Infection Control Officer within 1 hour via the incident-reporting system.

items.question: How many linked infection cases trigger automatic escalation to the Hospital Safety Committee?
items.reference_answer: A suspected cluster of three or more linked cases escalates automatically to the Hospital Safety Committee.

items.question: What two identifiers must be verified before medication administration?
items.reference_answer: Staff must verify at least two identifiers: full name and date of birth. Room number is not acceptable.

items.question: What must a nurse do immediately after a patient fall, in order?
items.reference_answer: Assess for injury, notify the attending physician, complete an incident report within 1 hour, and reassess fall risk before leaving the patient unattended again.

items.question: Which medications require an independent double-check by a second nurse?
items.reference_answer: High-alert medications such as insulin, anticoagulants, and opioids require independent double-check by a second licensed nurse before administration.

items.question: Who is responsible for leading the surgical time-out checklist?
items.reference_answer: The circulating nurse leads the verbal time-out checklist; the surgeon must verbally confirm each item before the first incision.

items.question: How quickly must the laboratory notify a clinician of a critical lab value?
items.reference_answer: The laboratory must notify the ordering clinician or covering nurse within 30 minutes of a critical value being verified.

items.question: What elements must be documented for informed surgical consent?
items.reference_answer: Consent must document the diagnosis, the proposed procedure, material risks and benefits, reasonable alternatives, and the consequences of declining treatment.

items.question: Who may obtain consent for an incapacitated adult with no healthcare proxy or spouse available?
items.reference_answer: Consent follows the order: healthcare proxy, then spouse, then adult child, then parent.

items.question: What happens when a patient refuses blood products on religious grounds?
items.reference_answer: A documented refusal must trigger a bloodless-medicine care-plan consult per the compliance manual, requested within 4 hours.

items.question: Under what condition can treatment proceed without prior consent?
items.reference_answer: When a patient faces an immediate, life-threatening emergency, cannot consent, and no legally authorized representative is immediately available, treatment necessary to prevent death or serious harm may proceed without prior consent.

items.question: Within what time must a suspected PHI breach be reported to the Compliance Officer?
items.reference_answer: A suspected PHI breach must be reported to the Compliance Officer within 1 hour of discovery.

items.question: What is required before withdrawing a controlled substance from the dispensing cabinet?
items.reference_answer: Controlled substances must be stored in a locked automated dispensing cabinet requiring two-factor identification for withdrawal.

items.question: What is the minimum nurse-to-patient ratio in the intensive care unit?
items.reference_answer: The minimum ratio in the intensive care unit is 1:2.

items.question: How soon must the resuscitation team arrive at the bedside after a Code Blue is activated?
items.reference_answer: The designated resuscitation team must arrive at the bedside within 3 minutes of activation, facility-wide.

items.question: What must staff do immediately after a sharps injury?
items.reference_answer: Wash the injury site with soap and water immediately and report to Occupational Health within 1 hour.

items.question: What is the hand-hygiene protocol before a procedure, and who audits compliance with it?
items.reference_answer: Before an invasive or aseptic procedure, staff must perform surgical hand antisepsis with a chlorhexidine-based scrub for at least 2 minutes, followed immediately by ABHR before glove donning. Compliance is audited monthly by the Infection Control Officer.

items.question: What is the hospital's approved dosage range for intravenous vancomycin in pediatric patients?
items.reference_answer: The corpus does not contain vancomycin dosing information; the assistant should abstain rather than fabricate a dosage.

items.question: Which parking garage is closest to the main hospital entrance?
items.reference_answer: The corpus does not cover facilities/parking information; the assistant should abstain as out of scope.
